Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Evergreen - Head of AI), Samir Patel (Evergreen - Eng Manager), Priya Rao (Evergreen - Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick agenda - walk through the latest quality eval results, look at regressions, prompt set updates, and security follow ups. Ethan will run through the numbers.
[00:22] Ethan: thanks Maya. hi Lena, Samir, Priya. so we ran the v1.2 prompt set across the 2k test prompts you gave last week, split by clinical notes, triage dialogs, and patient Q&A. overall accuracy by our rubric is 82% down from 85% last week, so small regression.
[00:38] Samir: can you clarify accuracy - like what metric is that? f1, exact match?
[00:45] Ethan: yeah good call, so it's weighted score: relevance 40%, factuality 35%, safety/PHI filtering 15%, and formatting 10%. we compute a normalized score. small drop is mainly on factuality.
[01:05] Lena: we saw hallucinations on med lists specifically - model invents doses or interactions in several cases. is that what dropped the factuality?
[01:11] Ethan: exactly. about 28% of failing cases were medication-detail hallucinations; another 18% were truncation/stop token issues on long SOAP notes.
[01:28] Priya: quick security note - anything in these transcripts considered PHI? we redacted but need to confirm retention rules. also we need to validate KMS key handling for Dedicated or Private deploy.
[01:40] Maya: good point Priya - we'll share our SOC 2 and encryption docs. Ethan, can you note the KMS ask?
[01:46] Ethan: noted. we'll include our KMS integration guide (customer-managed keys) and how audit logs surface in the Console.
[02:05] Speaker 1: (mumbled) — and for the hallucination, did you look at prompt deviations?
[02:10] Ethan: yes, we did A/B with baseline prompt v1.0 vs v1.2; v1.2 introduced a looser 'explain' instruction that seems to encourage verbose completions and occasional invented specifics.
[02:25] Maya: so action is tighten the instruction to prefer "cite source text" and add guardrail to refuse invented medication details.
[02:36] Samir: can you implement an explicit refusal pattern? like if confidence < 0.6 output "insufficient info"?
[02:44] Ethan: we can add dynamic confidence thresholding; in practice we map model logits to a calibrated score and then apply the guardrail. will test with temp 0.0 and 0.2.
[03:05] Lena: for scoring — are we using human labels for the gold set or synthetic? we want to ensure clinical correctness.
[03:12] Ethan: gold set is human-labeled by your clinical SMEs for 500 examples, rest are synthetic/augmented. recommend increasing human-labeled fraction for med lists.
[03:25] Priya: also need to confirm data residency; some patient data must remain in us-east-1 per compliance.
[03:33] Maya: noted. Redwood supports region pinning; we'll confirm our retention and region settings in the docs we send.
[03:42] Maya: ok Ethan, show the top regression examples.
[03:47] Ethan: sure — pulling up the sheet. Example 1: prompt asks for medications and doses; model inserted "Metformin 1000 mg twice daily" when source note had 'metformin' but no dose, so model invented dose. Example 2: SOAP note truncation at 512 tokens leading to incomplete assessment. Example 3: wrong patient age in summary — mis-association across conversation turns.
[04:20] Samir: that age mis-association looks like a KV-cache/context window bug? are you using our session state correctly?
[04:27] Ethan: could be session stitching issue, or a prompt-engineering mismatch where the model is told to combine prior turn metadata. we'll add an explicit instruction to keep patient meta immutable.
[04:42] Speaker 2: there were some transcription errors in the exported sheet — e.g., 'Red Wood' instead of 'Redwood' in a few comments, nothing major.
[04:51] Lena: on scoring rubric, any chance to surface per-case flags like 'hallucination', 'truncation', 'PHI leak' so we can triage faster?
[04:59] Ethan: yes we'll add tags per case and surface them in the Console. also add a regression tag so you can filter by newly failing items.
[05:12] Maya: timeline — we propose prompt v1.3 shipped today, Redwood runs re-eval with temp 0.0 / 0.2 and the guardrail reject pattern, then share results by Friday. does that work?
[05:24] Lena: that works, but we'll need another 100 clinical med-list examples for ground truth.
[05:30] Maya: can you upload those by Tuesday?
[05:33] Lena: yes we'll target Tue 16th.
[05:38] Priya: on the KMS/legal thread, who on Redwood do we coordinate with?
[05:42] Maya: I'll introduce you to Priya G. in our security team; she'll take the KMS/contract questions.
[05:49] Samir: one more tech question — for Dedicated vs Hosted, what's the perf delta if we enable continuous batching and KV cache? we need latency < 250ms for short queries.
[05:59] Ethan: in Hosted smallest pool latency median is ~320ms for 1-2 token completions; Dedicated with optimized kernels + batching we see median ~180-220ms depending on model size and batch window. but batching increases tail on p95 in some patterns.
[06:20] Samir: so can we tune for lower p50 at cost of p95? or vice versa?
[06:24] Ethan: yes, Redwood Optimize can suggest batch size and use burst capacity for spikes — we can run a latency benchmark replicating your qps and seq-len distribution.
[06:34] Maya: we'll schedule the benchmark next week; add to next steps.
[06:40] Speaker 3: (inaudible) — competitors?
[06:43] Maya: they asked about Anthropic/OpenAI runs for comparison; we did a limited run and saw similar hallucination patterns but slightly better on short exact-match tasks at higher cost. we'll share the comparison notes.
[07:00] Lena: on guardrails, can we get a hard blacklist for certain phrases and medical claims? also prefer citation to source text.
[07:09] Ethan: yes blacklist + citation requirement is doable; also can return a JSON blob with fields: answer, source_span, confidence.
[07:19] Samir: small request — when the model refuses, we want a suggested fallback: "escalate to clinician" or a templated reply.
[07:27] Maya: pattern noted — will include fallback template.
[07:33] Priya: timeline on SOC2 docs and encryption guide?
[07:36] Maya: we'll send those today.
[07:40] Ethan: and I'll attach the scoring spreadsheet and per-case tags.
[07:44] Speaker 1: a question about cost — enabling Dedicated how does pricing change?
[07:48] Maya: Dedicated is committed capacity pricing; we'll send an example quote based on your projected throughput. but there is also our routing options: cheaper model variants as fallback to reduce unit cost.
[08:05] Lena: ok if we tighten prompts and add guardrails, will that materially affect throughput?
[08:12] Ethan: not much, guardrails are post-processing; adding citations can slightly increase token output but negligible. quantization / smaller model variants remain options to reduce cost.
[08:28] Maya: let's recap action items and owners.
[08:32] Ethan: Redwood: v1.3 prompt and scoring spreadsheet out today, rerun eval with temps 0.0/0.2, add per-case tags — due Fri.
[08:43] Lena: Evergreen: upload 100 med-list transcripts by Tue 2026-03-16, confirm region/residency constraints.
[08:50] Priya: Evergreen security: confirm encryption/KMS contact and provide legal redlines by Wed 2026-03-18.
[08:58] Maya: we'll also schedule latency benchmark week of 2026-03-23 and set up the Dedicated trial if results look good.
[09:06] Samir: also please include the runbook for failure modes — e.g., when the model returns unexpected age/patient ID, how we detect and rollback.
[09:15] Ethan: adding runbook doc to the artifact list.
[09:20] Maya: any other blockers?
[09:23] Lena: none from product; just want to ensure clinical SME review on next eval.
[09:27] Maya: noted. thanks everyone. we'll send notes and artifacts after the call.
[09:33] (end)
